title: 2 Kings 21–25; 2 Chronicles 33–36; Jeremiah; Ezekiel; Daniel; Ezra; Nehemiah; Esther; Haggai; Zechariah — biblical text and canonical geography
license: CC0 / public domain according to project research supplied 2026-08-29
verifiedAt: 2026-08-29 — licensing status supplied by user research; official-source release check still recommended
notes: Primary source for biblical narrative sequence and place-names. Literary settings and theological claims are not automatically converted into independently verified historical events or precise modern coordinates.

title: Batch 6 Exile, Babylon, Persia & Restoration Curation Methodology
notes: Separates biblical narrative, securely dated imperial history, archaeological site identification, ancient inscriptions/tablets, literary setting, and reconstructed routes. Deportation and return lines visualize named endpoints and plausible corridors rather than recovered itineraries.

title: The Fall and Rise of Jerusalem: Judah under Babylonian Rule
author: Oded Lipschits
notes: Historical and archaeological synthesis for Judah between the Babylonian conquest and early Persian period; used conservatively for demographic and administrative context.

title: II Kings: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary
author: Mordechai Cogan and Hayim Tadmor
notes: Reference for late-monarchy chronology, Assyrian/Babylonian context, and textual geography.

title: The Book of Jeremiah
author: J. A. Thompson
organization: New International Commentary on the Old Testament
notes: Used for Jeremiah narrative geography and historical setting; exact site identifications remain independently classified.

title: Babylonian Chronicle concerning the early years of Nebuchadnezzar II (BM 21946 / Chronicle 5)
organization: Neo-Babylonian cuneiform chronicle; standard scholarly editions/translations
dateLabel: Early sixth century BCE; records campaigns including the capture of Jerusalem in 597 BCE
notes: Primary extra-biblical chronological evidence for the 605 BCE Carchemish campaign sequence and Nebuchadnezzar’s capture of Jerusalem in 597 BCE. The tablet is not a biblical text and is treated independently.

title: Babylonian ration tablets naming Yaukin/Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and members of his household
dateLabel: Sixth century BCE, during the Babylonian exile
notes: Administrative evidence for the exiled Judean king and royal household in Babylonia; it does not narrate Jerusalem’s fall.

title: Lachish Ostraca / Letters
organization: Late Iron Age Hebrew ostraca from Lachish
dateLabel: Early sixth century BCE, commonly associated with the final Babylonian crisis
notes: Primary epigraphic evidence from Judah near the end of the monarchy. Letter 4 famously mentions watching for Lachish signals and not seeing Azekah, but precise historical synchronization is interpreted cautiously.

title: Ketef Hinnom silver amulets
dateLabel: Late seventh to early sixth century BCE in common archaeological dating
notes: Silver amulets bearing wording closely related to the priestly blessing. They provide important evidence for pre-exilic/later Iron Age textual and religious context without identifying a biblical owner.

title: The Book of Ezekiel, Volumes 1–2
author: Daniel I. Block
organization: New International Commentary on the Old Testament
notes: Reference for Ezekiel’s chronology, Babylonian setting, visions, and the Kebar/Tel-abib geography. Visionary locations are kept distinct from ordinary terrestrial coordinates.

title: Documents of Judean Exiles and West Semites in Babylonia / Al-Yahudu archive scholarship
organization: Published Neo-Babylonian and Achaemenid cuneiform tablets
notes: Documents Judean communities integrated into rural Babylonian economic life. The exact findspot of Al-Yahudu is not securely known, so the atlas does not pin it as a modern archaeological site.

title: Daniel: A Commentary on the Book of Daniel
author: John J. Collins
notes: Critical reference for the literary and historical settings of Daniel. The atlas maps named imperial places while clearly separating literary setting from external corroboration of individual court narratives.

title: Nabonidus Chronicle
dateLabel: Sixth century BCE; records events surrounding the Persian conquest of Babylon in 539 BCE
notes: Primary evidence for the fall of Babylon to Cyrus’s forces. It does not mention Daniel or the biblical banquet narrative.

title: Cyrus Cylinder
dateLabel: After Cyrus II’s conquest of Babylon, 539 BCE
notes: Royal inscription describing Cyrus’s restoration of cults and displaced divine images/communities in Babylonian ideological language. It does not mention Judah, Jerusalem, the Judeans, or the Jerusalem temple by name.

title: Behistun Inscription of Darius I
dateLabel: Late sixth century BCE, early reign of Darius I
notes: Primary royal evidence for Darius I’s accession, revolts, and imperial ideology. Used for Persian imperial context, not as direct evidence for Haggai or Zechariah.

title: From Cyrus to Alexander: A History of the Persian Empire
author: Pierre Briant
notes: Major historical synthesis for Achaemenid institutions, chronology, royal centers, and western imperial administration.

title: The Persian Empire: A Corpus of Sources from the Achaemenid Period
author: Amélie Kuhrt
notes: Sourcebook for Achaemenid history used to cross-check royal chronology and imperial context.

title: Ezra, Nehemiah
author: H. G. M. Williamson
notes: Reference for Persian-period Judah, return traditions, Ezra/Nehemiah chronology, geography, and the uncertainty surrounding Ezra’s absolute date.

title: A History of the Jews and Judaism in the Second Temple Period, Volume 1: Yehud
author: Lester L. Grabbe
notes: Historical synthesis for Persian-period Yehud, administrative structures, social history, and source criticism.

title: Esther
author: Adele Berlin
notes: Reference for Esther’s Persian court setting, language, literary features, and the common identification of Ahasuerus with Xerxes I; individual narrative events are not claimed as independently attested.

title: Susa archaeological and Achaemenid palace scholarship
notes: Used for the secure location of Susa and its Achaemenid palace complex. The atlas does not identify a specific excavated room as the scene of an Esther episode.

title: Elephantine Aramaic papyri and letters
organization: Fifth-century BCE Jewish/Judean diaspora documents from Elephantine
dateLabel: Fifth century BCE; temple petition correspondence includes 407 BCE
notes: Independent evidence for a Judean/Jewish community and temple at Elephantine under Persian rule. This is historical context rather than a biblical narrative episode.

title: Ramat Rahel archaeological research — Babylonian and Persian-period administrative center
organization: Modern archaeological excavation and publication tradition
notes: Used conservatively for the important administrative complex south of Jerusalem. The site is not assigned a named biblical governor without inscriptional evidence.

title: Neo-Assyrian royal inscriptions naming Manasseh of Judah
notes: Assyrian royal lists include Manasseh, king of Judah, among western vassal rulers. This independently anchors Manasseh in the Assyrian imperial world without confirming every detail of 2 Kings or 2 Chronicles.

title: Babylonian Chronicle of the Fall of Nineveh (commonly ABC 3 / BM 21901)
dateLabel: Records the 612 BCE capture and destruction of Nineveh
notes: Primary Mesopotamian evidence for the coalition campaign that ended Nineveh as the Neo-Assyrian royal capital. It is historical context for Nahum, not proof of the date of composition of the book.

title: Nahum, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah: A Commentary
author: J. J. M. Roberts
notes: Used for the historical-literary setting and geographic references of the late seventh-century prophetic corpus; exact composition dates remain debated.

title: Obadiah: A New Translation with Introduction and Commentary
author: Paul R. Raabe
notes: Reference for Obadiah’s Edom/Jerusalem geography and the long-standing debate over its historical setting and date.
